chunks: 856 - And he said in another hadith that he mentioned to him:
Then face the Qiblah with your face, and do not turn your face away from the Qiblah, lest your salat become invalid. For Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says to His Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله:
"So turn your face toward al-Masjid al-Haram, and wherever you are, turn your faces toward it."

So stand upright." For the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: "Whoever does not straighten his spine, then there is no salat for him. And be humble with your gaze for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and do not raise it to the sky; rather let it be before your face at the place of your sajdah."

key_terms.الْقِبْلَةَ: the direction faced in ritual prayer
key_terms.صَلَاتُكَ: your salat, whose validity is being discussed
key_terms.صُلْبَهُ: his spine or back, meaning proper bodily straightness in standing

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith teach about facing the Qiblah and proper posture in salat?
ai.summary: This hadith instructs the worshipper to face the Qiblah steadily in obligatory salat, stand upright, and avoid movements that invalidate the prayer. It also links these rulings to the Qur'anic command of facing al-Masjid al-Haram and to the Prophetic teaching of proper posture and humble gaze during worship.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.856 - In another narration, the Imam said :
"Then turn your face toward the Qiblah and do not turn your face away from the Qiblah, lest your prayer become invalid. Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, says to His Prophet in the obligatory prayer:
'Turn your face toward the Sacred Mosque (Surah Al-Baqarah 2:144); and wherever you are, turn your faces toward it.' Stand upright."
The Prophet (sw) said: "Whoever does not straighten their spine (while standing) has no prayer."
And lower your gaze in humility before Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic; do not raise it to the sky. Let your gaze be directed in front of you toward your place of prostration”.
